entries.title: Chicago-area skydiver dies after mid-air collision in Southern California
entries.summary: <p>A Chicago-area skydiver was among two people killed after a mid-air collision Friday morning in Southern California. </p><p>Levi Pimentel, 29, of Aurora, was one of two women who died in the accident, according to the Riverside County Sheriff's Office. The second woman was identified as Georgia Jean, 56, from Box Elder, South Dakota.</p><p>The incident happened around noon PST Friday when Pimentel and Jean were about 150 feet from the ground as their parachutes became entangled, Skydive Elsinore, a skydiving company hosting the event where the incident happened, said in a statement. </p><p>Both women were taken to area hospitals where they were pronounced dead, officials said. There were no reports of malfunctioning equipment. </p><p>Pimentel and Jean were both licensed skydivers visiting for the event, according to Skydive Elsinore.</p><p>Pimentel has spent nearly nine years employed at iFly Indoor Skydiving in Naperville in various roles, including lead trainer, lead instructor and flight instructor, according to her LinkedIn page. </p><p>She previously worked as a skydiving instructor at Sky Nights SPC, based in East Troy, Wisconsin. </p><p>"Skydive Elsinore extends its deepest condolences to the families, friends and loved ones of both skydivers, and is grieving alongside all those affected," the company said in the statement. </p>

entries.title: Providence flashes a multidimensional offense in 5A win against Morgan Park
entries.summary: <p>With Broden Mackert healthy again and DeAngelo Coates coming into his own, Providence just keeps getting more multidimensional on offense.</p><p>The Celtics leaned on the running of Mackert and Brayden McKay, the passing of Dominic Vita and the pass-catching of Coates and John Cullen on Saturday as they held off Morgan Park 42-34 in the second round of the Class 5A playoffs at Stagg Stadium.</p><p>Junior quarterback Ronald Smith Jr. had a huge day for the Mustangs, passing for 405 yards and four touchdowns.</p><p>After its second consecutive victory against a ranked team, Providence (9-3) will play Carbondale (10-2) in the quarterfinals next weekend.</p><p>Mackert was sidelined by injury late in the regular season, but the senior is back on his typically heavy workload. Against Kankakee last week and Morgan Park, Mackert piled up more than 400 rushing yards and six touchdowns.</p><p>He had three against the Mustangs (9-2), including scores of 48 and 45 yards, as the Celtics built a 29-point lead before surviving a furious rally.</p><p>McKay added a touchdown run, Vita threw a 42-yard touchdown pass to Cullen and Coates caught four passes for 87 yards to keep Providence’s offense rolling.</p><p>‘‘We’re not a passing school,’’ said Coates, a 6-4 junior. ‘‘So when we pass the ball, every opportunity I get, it’s an honor.’’</p><p>‘‘He’s a weapon, man,’’ Celtics interim coach Adam Nissen said of Coates. ‘‘Tall, can run, stretches the defenses vertically for us. He has matured a ton since last year.’’</p><p>Mackert said he appreciates the attention Coates and the rest of Providence’s receivers attract from opposing defenses.</p><p>‘‘It’s great,’’ Mackert said. ‘‘It makes defenses scheme around everybody. O-line, they do their job. . . . Having Dom Vita as our quarterback and all the receivers being [a] threat — I mean, the defense has got to take time on that, not just the run game. So it’s good for us.’’</p><p>The game was scoreless until McKay’s one-yard touchdown run midway through the second quarter. Providence then scored three touchdowns in a span of 96 seconds — all after Morgan Park turnovers, starting with Isaac Patton’s 53-yard scoop-and-score — to make it 28-0 at halftime.</p><p>Jonsean Young got the Mustangs’ comeback started with the first of his two touchdowns, a 56-yard run early in the third, but the Celtics’ lead peaked at 35-6 on the second of Mackert’s three touchdowns.</p><p>Smith and Morgan Park kept plugging away, however, scoring 28 points in the last 14 minutes to make it a game.</p><p>The bottom line for Providence is it beat two quality opponents to reach the final eight in 5A.</p><p>‘‘We saw the draw right away, and we kind of welcome it,’’ Nissen said. ‘‘Our thought process is we have to see them at some point eventually, so let’s knock them out round whatever, round one and round two.’’</p><p>Mustangs coach Chris James liked his team’s fight after falling into the big hole.‘‘I challenged the kids at halftime about [giving] 24 minutes of maximum effort,’’ he said. ‘‘The turnovers, they hurt us. And we had a few misses at the end of the half that could have really put us in a good position. When you get in a game like this, you can’t do that.’</p>

entries.title: Marion Persich runs for 183 yards as Morris dominates Montini in long-awaited 4A playoff showdown
entries.summary: <p>High school football is Morris's pride and joy. The Warriors are undefeated this season, led by bruising, physical quarterback Marion Persich.</p><p>The team, and the entire football-crazed town, have spent a year preparing for another crack at Montini. The Broncos, led by Israel Abrams, knocked Morris out of the Class 4A playoffs last year.</p><p>“I’ll be honest, the second we started lifting in the offseason, daily, we started talking about these guys,” Warriors coach Alan Thorson said. “We knew this game was coming. We were all Montini during the bye week. Last week we were 80% Montini.”</p><p>Abrams, a Miami recruit, arrived in Morris as the consensus No. 2 quarterback prospect in the country. But nothing went his way on <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/scores/2026/11/06/2026-ihsa-state-football-second-round-playoff-scores" >Saturday</a>. </p><p>Abrams left with an injury in the third quarter with Morris leading by 14, and the Warriors went on to win the second round <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/10/17/ihsa-state-football-playoff-pairings-class4a-illinois-2026" >Class 4A</a> playoff game 41-7.</p><p>“Yeah, they have a five-star quarterback,” Persich said. “I might not have all that many offers, but I am going to come out here and give it my all, and I’m going to play with all my heart.”</p><p>Persich had 22 carries for 182 yards and two touchdowns. He completed 6 of 9 passes for 142 yards. </p><p>Montini (8-3) stopped Persich three yards short of a touchdown to end the first half, but Morris opened the third quarter with a dominant, all-run drive, and Persich scored on a one-yard run to give the Warriors a 21-7 lead.</p><p>Abrams, who led Montini to the 4A title last year and the 3A championship in 2024, was injured a few minutes later. He was sacked in the backfield and fumbled the ball away to Morris (11-0).</p><p>“He has had a rib injury, and he hasn’t been 100% for a few weeks,” Montini coach Mike Bukovsky said. “He got cracked pretty good in the ribs, and on top of that he got his ankle twisted. The ankle was not as serious of a thing, but he was struggling to breathe for a little bit there.”</p><p>Senior lineman Carter Snyder blew up Montini’s first play from scrimmage with a tackle for loss, setting the tone. Senior Jackson Knapp and Snyder both added sacks later in the game.</p><p>“That’s how we are,” Morris lineman Brady Armstrong said. “We are a hard-nosed football team. entries.title: Fire fall to Crew in regular-season finale
entries.summary: <p>Gonzalo Tapia netted a pair of goals and Brais Méndez scored the winner in stoppage time to help the Columbus Crew pull out a 4-3 Decision Day victory over the Chicago Fire on Saturday.</p><p>Columbus (14-15-5) trailed three times before rallying to avoid the Eastern Conference wild-card match. The Crew jumped from ninth place to seventh after FC Cincinnati lost 2-0 to Nashville SC. Columbus will play No. 2 seed Inter Miami in the best-of-three first round.</p><p>Despite the loss, Chicago (16-11-7) finished fourth in the East and earned the home-field advantage in a first-round matchup with Charlotte FC.</p><p>Robert Lewandowski gave Chicago a 1-0 lead in the 8th minute on a penalty kick. The 38-year-old's eighth goal through his first 19 MLS appearances came after a foul on Columbus midfielder Sekou Bangoura.</p><p>The Crew tied it in the 16th minute when Tapia used assists from Taha Habroune and Santiago Rodríguez to score his fifth goal through his first 11 league matches. Habroune's assist was his career-high fifth, and Rodríguez notched his eighth in 12 appearances this season.</p><p>Lewandowski scored on another penalty kick in the 22nd minute to put the Fire back in front after another foul on Bangoura.</p><p>Anass Zaroury tied it 2-2 a minute later with an unassisted goal — his third in his first eight matches, all starts.</p><p>Chicago took a 3-2 lead into halftime when Maren Haile-Selassie scored unassisted in the fourth minute of stoppage time. Haile-Selassie posted career highs of 13 goals and 10 assists this season.</p><p>Tapia scored again in the 62nd minute to tie it 3-all. Habroune collected another assist and defender Malte Amundsen picked one up, giving him three in each of the last four seasons.</p><p>Méndez finished his first regular season with six goals and four assists in 14 appearances with 10 starts.</p><p>Patrick Schulte stopped three shots for the Crew, who close out the regular season on a 6-0-1 unbeaten streak.</p><p>Chris Brady totaled two saves for Fire, who entered play 2-0-1 in their previous three matches.</p><p>The two clubs played to a scoreless draw in Ohio to begin March.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Columbus: Hits the road to begin the series with Inter Miami.</p><p>Chicago: Hosts No.. 5 seed Charlotte in first-round opener.</p>

entries.title: Pressure mounting on Kyle Davidson to make changes after Blackhawks' atrocious 9-2 loss
entries.summary: <p>RALEIGH, N.C. — The existing mountain of pressure on <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> general manager Kyle Davidson to make changes to the team this week grew to the size of Mt. Everest on Saturday.</p><p>An awful-beyond-words 9-2 loss to the Hurricanes made it exceedingly clear the Hawks cannot play another game in their current form.</p><p>Entering this difficult southern road trip, the four-day break in the schedule that has now arrived <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/03/blackhawks-changes-trip-kyle-davidson-jeff-blashill" >looked like</a> a possible boiling point. After going 0-3 on the trip and concluding it with their most lopsided defeat in almost three years, that water is now veritably boiling.</p><p>The only questions concern what Davidson will do and when he'll do it. </p><p>Saturday certainly looked like the kind of game that can get a coach fired, for one thing, although coach Jeff Blashill said afterward that he isn't thinking about his job security.</p><p>He said he believes there's trust between him and the players and between him and management. But he acknowledged this four-day break needs to be significant, one way or another.</p><p>"We've got to make this a bottom point in the year, and we've got to find a way to claw our way out of this," Blashill said.</p><p>"Is there any tweak to anything we do that can put our guys in a better position to win games? We'll look at that tonight. Not that we haven't, but we'll certainly do a deep dive tonight into tomorrow and see if there's any kind of solutions that we can give to these guys."</p><h3><b>Trades, too?</b></h3><p>Trades involving the playing roster seem both necessary and likely, too. </p><p>Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Saturday the Hawks have become very active on the trade market, shopping the the Oilers' and Panthers' first-round picks they own as well as their plethora of second-round picks.</p><p>Friedman also mentioned pending free agents Teuvo Teravainen and Jordan Greenway are being shopped, presumably to make room for guys brought in.</p><p>The Hawks still have more than three quarters of the season left, and they certainly could use an injection of talent to at least deliver a respectable product during that span. </p><p>But at 4-13-1, they've already dug a hole so deep that it's fair to whether it would be wise to invest any more assets into this current season.</p><h3><b>Atrocious effort</b></h3><p>Blashill has defended the Hawks' effort levels after most of their losses this season, but he didn't Saturday. Nor did Connor Bedard, who called it an "embarrassing" loss.</p><p>The Hawks made basically every mistake possible and, on a few Hurricanes goals, seemed to either forget basic fundamentals of hockey or even stop trying altogether. </p><p>The Hurricanes' third, fifth and sixth goals were particularly egregious from a Hawks perspective. On the third, the fourth line of Jordan Greenway, Dillon Boucher and Cole Smith attempted the least effective 2-1-2 forecheck of all time, which the Hurricanes carved up immediately to get a two-on-one rush that Jordan Martinook finished off.</p><p>On the fifth, Roman Kantserov committed an inexcusable defensive-zone turnover, Tyler Bertuzzi and Bedard were burned for lazy stick-based defense and Artyom Levshunov and Alex Vlasic made little effort to stop Andrei Svechnikov from burying his own rebound.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Canes goal: Andrei Svechnikov walks past Bertuzzi and makes it 5-0. <a href="https://t.co/QbQVsBrj3E">pic.twitter.com/QbQVsBrj3E</a></p>— BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) <a href="https://x.com/BlackhawksFocus/status/2119251402560053655?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 8, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>On the sixth, Kaiser made a terrible decision pass into the slot with three Hawks forwards deep and three Hurricanes in the way, creating an instant two-on-one rush that Sebastian Aho finished off. That made it 6-0 barely halfway through the game.</p><p>The Hawks held a players-only meeting after the final horn in which they vented frustrations, floated ideas for changes and tried to "get to the reality" of the current situation, Kaiser said.</p><p>"There’s frustration all the time when you’re waking up, when you’re going to bed, you’re thinking about the record and the hole that we’re in," said Bedard, who's facing his own mountain of adversity just two months into his captaincy.</p><p>"What we’ve been able to do really well is every practice, every pregame skate, every lunch, [every] dinner, every time we hang out, we still have that camaraderie and have that joy to be at the rink. But at the end of the day, it’s a results league, and we’ve got to be better. There's nothing else to do it."</p><p>For now, the Hawks are scheduled to have a day off Sunday and practice Monday before the annual season-ticket member party that night.</p>

entries.title: Notre Dame knocks off top-ranked Miami
entries.summary: <p>SOUTH BEND, Ind. — Marcus Freeman didn't deny the obvious. Even for a storied program like Notre Dame, beating Miami had enormous significance.</p><p>If that wasn't enough, it kept Notre Dame's national title hopes alive as well.</p><p>CJ Carr threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns, and No. 4 Notre Dame avenged its most damaging loss from last season by running out to a 21-point lead and holding on to beat No. 1 Miami 31-24 on Saturday night.</p><p>Micah Gilbert caught two of Carr's scoring passes, Jordan Faison had the other and Nolan James Jr. had a rushing score for Notre Dame (8-1, No. 11 College Football Playoff), which came into the game knowing another loss to Miami could doom its CFP chances.</p><p>“It’s a special moment,” said Freeman, Notre Dame's coach. “Enjoy the moment, because tomorrow when you wake up it’s time to get ready for the next one. I know it’s a big one. This is big. This is special. I’m not going to sit here and say this was like the other ones. No, this is different.”</p><p>The Hurricanes (8-1, No. 1 CFP) started slowly on offense in their first game without injured wide receiver and Heisman Trophy hopeful Malachi Toney — and Notre Dame, which lost to Miami 27-24 last season in a game that ultimately kept the Irish out of the playoff, never trailed.</p><p>Darian Mensah threw three touchdown passes for Miami, twice getting the Hurricanes within a touchdown after they trailed 24-3 early in the third. Cooper Barkate had a pair of those scoring grabs, and Elija Lofton had the other.</p><p>“Proud of the guys, the way we fought back,” Mensah said. “Obviously, it wasn't enough.”</p><p>Lofton nearly had a touchdown catch that would have made it 31-30 — the score of the Miami-Notre Dame game in 1988 — with 3:36 left, appearing to make a fourth-down grab in the end zone and getting his feet down.</p><p>But Notre Dame's Luke Talich — who had an interception in the third quarter — knocked the ball away, with officials ruling that Lofton didn't complete the grab. Notre Dame took over on downs, ran the clock down to about a minute and held on from there.</p><p>Miami coach Mario Cristobal said he was “beyond upset” that Lofton's play wasn't ruled a score.</p><p>“Obviously, a tough loss to take,” Cristobal said. “Proud of our players for the resilience. ... Don't leave it in the hands of the officials. Play better. Coach better. Find a way to win.”</p><p>With Miami falling, only two unbeaten teams remain in the Football Bowl Subdivision — Utah and UCLA, which both moved to 9-0 on Saturday. This is the first time since 2003 that only two teams made it through the first nine games unbeaten; TCU and Oklahoma did it that year.</p><p>On a night when 43 NFL scouts were part of a jam-packed crowd at Notre Dame Stadium, where it was 40 degrees Fahrenheit at kickoff and fell into the mid-30s as the night went along, the Irish stayed true to their mantra for 2026 — one born from the frustration from not making the CFP field a year ago.</p><p>They left no doubt. It got a little shaky at the end, but the Irish's CFP hopes are very much alive.</p><p><b>The takeaway</b></p><p>Miami: Miami had first-and-goal from the Notre Dame 1 in the second quarter and wound up settling for a field goal, after three runs — one by Fletcher and two keepers by Mensah — went nowhere. The Hurricanes wound up trailing 17-3 at halftime, after scoring at least 14 points and averaging 27 first-half points in their first eight contests this season.</p><p>Notre Dame: The Irish pulled out all the stops, with a slew of former stars — Joe Montana, Jerome Bettis Sr., Tony Rice, Chris Zorich, Ricky Watters, Ron Pawlus and NBA President of Basketball Operations Byron Spruell among them — for on-field tributes. Also honored was Pat Murphy, the manager of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, who won 73% of his games when he coached at Notre Dame.</p><p><b>No. 1 things</b></p><p>Miami fell to 44-7 when playing as the No. 1 team in the AP Top 25, including an 0-2 mark against Notre Dame — after the top-ranked Hurricanes lost to the fourth-ranked Irish 31-30 in the “Catholics vs. Convicts” game in 1988.</p><p>Notre Dame improved to 10-17-1 against No. 1 teams, getting its first win in exactly six years. It beat No. 1 Clemson at home on Nov. 7, 2020, a game where the Tigers were without star quarterback Trevor Lawrence.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Miami: Hosts Duke next Saturday.</p><p>Notre Dame: Hosts Boston College next Saturday.</p>

entries.title: Northwestern has a rough showing in loss to Iowa
entries.summary: <p>Hank Brown threw for a touchdown and ran for another, and Braeden Jackson returned a kickoff for a TD for the second time this season as No. 21 Iowa beat Northwestern for the fifth straight time and dealt the Wildcats their first loss at the new Ryan Field in Evanston, 24-10 on Saturday night.</p><p>The Hawkeyes (7-2, 4-2 Big Ten) have allowed only two touchdowns in the past three games. They recorded six sacks and didn't allow the Wildcats inside their 26-yard line until the fourth quarter.</p><p>Brown was 16-of-21 passing for 126 yards with an interception after going 20 for 24 in last week's win over Wisconsin.</p><p>Northwestern has dropped two straight after a 6-1 start. The Wildcats (6-3, 3-3), who won twice at their temporary lakefront stadium before winning the first three games at their new $875 million home, were trying to move to 6-0 at home for the first time in 122 years.</p><p>Iowa, which scored on 98-yard drives in each of its previous two games, had a 97-yard drive Saturday.</p><p>“Just doing the good things, whether it's fourth-down stops or driving the ball and then putting it in the end zone. That's how you build confidence,” Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz said. “You can't give it to them. Doing it in practice is a start, but doing it in game competition against good teams, it's a good thing. Hopefully what they'll take from this is they have to do it every week.”</p><p>Brown was 4 for 4 on Iowa's opening possession before sprinting for a 21-yard touchdown on a quarterback draw. He found Tony Diaz for a 24-yard TD catch early in the second quarter to cap the 97-yard drive and make it 14-0 after L.J. Phillips had a 45-yard run to get the Hawkeyes near midfield.</p><p>Phillips, who ran for 1,920 yards at South Dakota last season, had his best game in an Iowa uniform with 128 yards on 21 carries and two catches for 14 yards.</p><p>Northwestern's Nicco Marchiol, a West Virginia transfer filling in for injured starter Aidan Chiles, was 24 of 32 for 181 yards and one touchdown to go with 52 yards rushing, but Iowa held Northwestern to 2.8 yards per carry and stuffed the Wildcats twice on third-and-1 and twice on fourth-and 1.</p><p>“We are not satisfied,” Northwestern coach David Braun said. “I’m not going to sit here and tell the group that our guys kept battling and I’m proud of it. We are not satisfied, I’m not satisfied, and our staff isn’t satisfied. But we also aren’t discouraged.”</p><p>Robert Fitzgerald picked off an underthrown pass by Brown midway through the third quarter to give the Wildcats some life, but the drive stalled and Northwestern settled for a 45-yard field goal from Jackson Kleather to break up the shutout.</p><p>Jackson returned the ensuing kickoff 96 yards to make it 21-3. He had a 99-yard touchdown return in Iowa's win at Michigan in September. Caden Buhr added a 52-yard field goal later in the third.</p><p>Marchiol connected with Joseph Hilmon II on a 2-yard touchdown pass with 1:51 to play.</p><p><b>Game ball for Campbell</b></p><p>Ferentz said the team would give a game ball to former Iowa and current Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, who suffered a spinal injury on Sunday.</p><p>“You're hearing some encouraging news," Ferentz said. "It's going to be I don't know how long a road but it's moving in the right direction so I thought that was really fitting to give him a ball and we'll get that to him. I'm just glad we won because otherwise you're kind of screwed, you know?”</p><p><b>The takeaway</b></p><p>Iowa: Linebacker Cam Buffington had 12 tackles to lead the Hawkeyes for the fifth time this season, his fourth game with double-digit tackles.</p><p>Northwestern: The Wildcats had been converting third downs at a 46% clip and were 5 for 7 on fourth down with the dual threat Chiles at quarterback this season, but Iowa held Northwestern to 1 for 11 on third down and 1 for 4 on fourth down.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Iowa hosts Purdue next Saturday.</p><p>Northwestern visits No. 11 Ohio State next Saturday.</p>

entries.title: What to watch for in Buccaneers-Bears game Sunday: A new test for the Bears' rebuilt defensive line
entries.summary: <p>What to watch for when <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a> host the Buccaneers on Sunday night:</p><h3>When the Bears have the ball</h3><p>Tight end Colston Loveland has been a much bigger part of the passing attack since quarterback Caleb Williams returned from injury. He finally is starting to look like the top-five tight end he was projected to be going into the season.</p><p>Loveland had only 23 targets and caught 13 passes for 110 yards and no touchdowns in the first five games. Since then, he has been the seventh-most targeted player in the NFL (28 in three games) and has 20 catches for 199 yards and two touchdowns. He still is lagging behind his numbers as a rookie last season, but look for his upward trend to continue.</p><p>The Buccaneers are No. 3 in total defense and the NFL’s best against the run, which might force the Bears to go to the air more. Coach Ben Johnson won’t ever bail on the ground game entirely, but it’s going to be tough to beat the Bucs that way, given that they allow 80 rushing yards per game and 3.6 per carry.</p><p>With Johnson sure to run enough to at least keep the Bucs’ defense honest, Loveland is an ideal chess piece. He’ll be in on plays that appear to be runs, signaling to defenders that he’s in to block, then theoretically get matchups against players who will have trouble keeping up with his speed. That’s an especially smart ploy in goal-to-go scenarios.</p><h3>When the Buccaneers have the ball</h3><p>The Bucs’ rushing attack presents a challenge for the Bears and will be a test for their revamped defensive line led by newcomer <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/05/new-bears-dt-jeffery-simmons-arrival-at-halas-hall-has-been-flawless-on-and-off-the-field" target="_blank" >Jeffery Simmons</a>. The Bucs lead the NFL with 168.6 rushing yards per game behind the tandem of Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell.</p><p>Irving is fourth in the league with 728 rushing yards (five yards per carry) and has five touchdown runs. Gainwell also averages five yards per carry in a lesser role.</p><p>The Bucs won their last game without completing a pass, the first team to do so since 1974, as they opted for a run-dominant attack in sloshy conditions against the Falcons. They averaged 5.8 yards per carry, despite the Falcons knowing what was coming.</p><p>In Simmons’ debut with the Bears on Monday, they shut down the Seahawks’ running game by holding Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet to a combined 52 yards on 16 carries.</p><p>They’re a shade behind the Bucs in run defense at 86.8 yards per game, third in the league, and the only foe to rush for 100 yards against them was the Vikings’ Aaron Jones.</p><p>The Bears have helped themselves by playing with a lead and controlling the clock. When an opponent is losing and running short on time, it has no choice but to throw.</p><p>That would be advantageous to the Bears, given that Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield is playing through a thumb injury on his throwing hand and is having one of the worst seasons of his career statistically.</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Crotchety father-in-law has run out of friends
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My husband, "Mark," and his father have a strained relationship due to things that occurred when Mark was growing up. Mark is an only child, and his mother has passed away. Since I met my father-in-law prior to our marriage eight years ago, he has never taken any interest in me, Mark or our children. While he has never been directly unkind to me, every time there is a conversation, he makes negative comments about my profession. (I'm a lawyer.)</p><p>I gather from our conversations that he seeks companionship online and has been scammed multiple times by the "friends" he makes. Abby, what are my duties as a daughter-in-law given the relationship? Mark rarely takes his father's calls or answers his questions, so he calls me for help.</p><p>Mark's dad has no one else — no siblings, no spouse, no other children and (from what I can tell) no friends. His requests and issues have become draining. I already have three small children who require most of my attention. I dread talking to him because of the inevitable jabs at lawyers, and he rarely takes my advice anyway. Do I need to keep answering his phone calls and texts? — <i>HAD IT IN NORTH DAKOTA</i></p><p><b>DEAR HAD IT:</b> No, you do not have to take your father-in-law's calls if his comments about lawyers offend you. What you do have to do is tell him his jokes are offensive and to cut it out. Then, if he doesn't apologize (and doesn't cut it out), tell your husband you are done dealing with his father and from now on he is going to have to be better about returning the man's phone calls.</p><p>Regarding the scams perpetrated by your FIL's online acquaintances, Mark may be able to find help without involving you if he contacts the North Dakota Health and Human Services Adult and Aging Division. (I doubt I needed to tell a lawyer that, but other readers may find it helpful.)</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My friends recently welcomed their first grandchild, but the child's parents won't allow photographs of the baby to be posted on social media until the child can consent. People naturally would love to see pics of the baby, but the parents' policy prevents it. Is this a new trend, or are these parents just weird? Would it be out of line for me to request a pic via email? I'd be happy to sign an NDA! — <i>QUESTIONING THE POLICY</i></p><p><b>DEAR QUESTIONING:</b> I wouldn't call it a new trend. The practice of keeping a child's images out of social media has been quite common for several years, and it's a policy I wholeheartedly endorse. Not only does posting baby pics violate the future privacy of the baby, but it also opens the family up to a shocking range of safety concerns, from identity theft and fraud to kidnapping.</p><p>Your request for an emailed image shouldn't cause offense; the worst that can happen is that they'll decline. If the parents agree to send you pictures, do not post them to your own socials. You will not enjoy the repercussions if you do.</p><p><i>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.</i></p>

entries.summary: <p>Joy filled Morris on Saturday night: fireworks, horns, and more. The town’s beloved Warriors had <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2026/11/07/marion-persich-runs-for-183-yards-as-morris-dominates-montini-in-long-awaited-4a-playoff-showdown" >knocked off Montini</a>, a private school powerhouse, in the Class 4A playoffs.</p><p>A similar scene likely played out at Downers Grove North, where the Trojans beat Catholic League power St. Rita in a 7A playoff showdown. Lincoln-Way West knocked off St. Laurence in another 7A matchup.</p><p>The three results were notable after much of the past week was spent debating IHSA bylaw proposals that would split public and private schools into separate state playoffs or give them separate paths into the state semifinals.</p><p>Here is Morris coach Alan Thorson, when asked if he wanted public vs. private playoff matchups to go away:</p><p>"If I am winning, I love it. I don’t even know how to answer that. We’ve lost some good ones to these guys and [Joliet Catholic]. But man, when you can beat them, it is such a special thing. What a great atmosphere. Credit to both schools and both communities. To play a game like this, in this environment, this is what high school football is all about.”</p><p>Morris fan Dane Zumbahlen made a pertinent point on X after the game:</p><p>“These games should not go away. You have to relish the opportunity like we did in ‘05 vs [Joliet Catholic]. You have to beat the best to be the best. They don’t always go your way, but it’s games like these that built Morris football.”</p><p>The Downers Grove North, Morris and Lincoln-Way West games are just three isolated results, however. I found it inspiring to see remnants of the neighborhood I used to live in recreated to tell his story.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/summer-festivals/2026/06/13/review-lil-uzi-vert-chief-keef-sexyy-red-and-g-herbo-day-one-summer-smash" >Lil Uzi Vert, Chief Keef, Sexyy Red and G Herbo deliver explosive sets on day one: Summer Smash review</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>After DJ Pharris and rapper/streamer/friend BenDaDonn warmed up the crowd, G Herbo hit the stage at around 9 p.m. Kicking off with the bone-chilling “At The Light”, “Kill S---,” and “4 Minutes of Hell,” bangers from his critically acclaimed debut mixtape “Welcome To Fazoland,” he sent a clear message that this show is strictly for the Day One fans as he performed each of his songs in chronological order.</p><p>“My pain is your pain. entries.title: Blackhawks' first change is at backup goalie: Arvid Soderblom placed on waivers
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a>' first change of hopefully <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/07/blackhawks-hurricanes-loss-kyle-davidson-jeff-blashill-pressure-changes" >many</a> this week came Sunday as backup goalie Arvid Soderblom was placed on waivers.</p><p>The move likely ends Soderblom's run of more than three seasons as the Hawks' backup, at least for now. The 27-year-old Swede is on the second year of a two-year contract and will be an unrestricted free agent next summer.</p><p>Once he clears waivers Monday — or gets claimed by another team — the Hawks will have a roster spot free to add a new goalie. </p><p>Presumably, that will be longtime prospect Drew Commesso, who has been patiently waiting his turn in Rockford for three-plus years now. He signed a new two-year contract this past summer that converts to a one-way deal next season.</p><p>Commesso has struggled early this season in the AHL, going 2-4-1 with an .890 save percentage, but he has proven himself a solid AHL goalie each of the past three seasons. He impressed in three NHL starts last season, too, going 2-1-0 with a .918 save percentage — including a heroic shutout against the Predators.</p><p>Soderblom, meanwhile, has long been a scapegoat for fans, who will likely welcome this move — while continuing to expect more significant ones in the coming days.</p><p>He has an .885 save percentage across 117 career NHL games, and he has been particularly poor early this season, losing each of his four starts and posting an .842 save percentage. He most recently allowed several soft goals that doomed the Hawks to a 4-1 loss <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/05/blackhawks-lightning-arvid-soderblom-backup-goalie" >Thursday</a> against the Lightning (then allowed three more goals in relief Saturday against the Hurricanes).</p><p>Since the start of last season, his minus-18.2 GSAA ranks sixth-worst in the NHL, per Natural Stat Trick. That means he has allowed 18.2 more goals than expected based on the quantity and quality of shots he has faced.</p><p>There's no guarantee Commesso turns out to be an improvement over Soderblom — particularly behind a defense this weak — but it's hard to imagine him being worse. It's almost certainly worth a shot.</p>

entries.title: Mike Tirico won't call Bears-Bucs game because of health issue
entries.summary: <p>NBC announcer Mike Tirico will not, in fact, call his 300<sup>th</sup> NFL game Sunday night.</p><p>Tirico said in a statement released around noon Sunday that a health issue will prevent him from calling the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Buccaneers</a>-<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/halas-intrigue" target="_blank" >Bears</a> game at Soldier Field. Noah Eagle will take his place alongside color analyst Cris Collinsworth and sideline reporter Melissa Stark.</p><p>“I look forward to watching tonight and can’t wait to be back with Cris, Melissa and the rest of our SNF team next Sunday night in Cincinnati,” he said.</p><p>Tirico has called NFL games for 20 years and has been the play-by-play announcer on NBC’s Sunday night broadcast since 2022. He’s called 299 regular season and playoff NFL games.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="zxx" dir="ltr"><a href="https://t.co/eKyVRb8ZOn">pic.twitter.com/eKyVRb8ZOn</a></p>— NBC Sports PR (@NBCSportsPR) <a href="https://x.com/NBCSportsPR/status/2119495623896400051?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 8, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Eagle won’t have to travel far — was the play-by-play announcer for NBC’s broadcast of Notre Dame’s win against No. 1 Miami on Saturday night in South Bend, Ind.</p><p>The Bears-Bucs game kicks off at 7:20 p.m.</p>

entries.title: Maybe 450,000 Lollapalooza fans trampling Grant Park every year isn't such a good idea
entries.summary: <p>The 1933 Century of Progress International Exposition worked so well, between the Graf Zeppelin floating by and Sally Rand, with her naughty bubble dance, many Chicagoans never wanted it to leave.</p><p>They extended the fair for an extra season in 1934, then wondered: why not keep the party going? Mayor Edward J. Kelly proposed building a sprawling lakefront pleasure center — a "wonderland" of exhibition halls, picnic shelters, public beaches, an ice skating rink, a casino, and a big parking garage. Paid for by the federal government, of course.</p><p>There are some funny moments in the "Secret Diary of Harold Ickes," where Franklin D. Roosevelt's penny-pinching secretary of the interior, a University of Chicago graduate, dismisses Kelly's dreams of a "Coney Island" on the lakefront, warning FDR that a significant chunk of any federal money thrown at the plan would end up in the pockets of the Kelly-Nash Democratic machine.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-880000" name="module-880000"></a> <div class="RichTextSidebarModule-title">Opinion bug</div> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h2>Opinion</h2></div> </div><p>Still, Kelly's dream was not far-fetched. The site where this wonderland was to be built became McCormick Place, and having a vast hall — then two — has been a magnet drawing exhibition business to Chicago: all those auto, electronics, restaurant and houseware shows. </p><p>With the historic fireworks coming from last week's election, you could be forgiven for overlooking that more than two-third of Chicago voters — 68% — said "yes" on the referendum question: “Should Chicago develop a permanent festival and outdoor event space for large-scale events?”</p><p>Hell yes. The result isn't binding, but makes sense. Venues lure business. As it is now, big music festivals hijack public spaces not only while they're going on, but during lengthy preparation and even lengthier clean-up. Repairing Grant Park after Lollapalooza took a month. Restoring the damage after this year's rain-soaked Riot Fest in Douglass Park might take until Thanksgiving. Yes, the festivals cover clean-up expenses — topping $1 million with Lolla —but that adds to the already astronomical ticket prices. One assumes a dedicated festival space would suffer less costly damage.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a The stir-'em-up columnist in me wants to suggest the city put the permanent entertainment venue on the Sydney Marovitz Golf Course — 71 acres of prime lakefront property. Golf is struggling to stay popular anyway. But I would never suggest that, first because I don't want to hear from aggrieved golfers. entries.title: Man charged in fatal shooting during family argument in Greater Grand Crossing
entries.summary: <p>A 59-year-old man was charged with first-degree murder following a fatal September shooting in Greater Grand Crossing, Chicago police said. </p><p>Coleman Jeffrey, 59, was arrested on Friday in Greater Grand Crossing. He's accused of fatally shooting Mark Hurn, 54, on Sept. 27 in the 500 block of East 76th Street. </p><p>At the time, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/28/family-spat-leaves-man-fatally-shot-in-greater-grand-crossing" target="_blank" >police said the shooting</a> stemmed from a family argument. A witness told officers the fight was about the shooter and the care of his mother. Hurn was the boyfriend of the alleged shooter's sister. He was shot in his chest, abdomen and legs.</p><p>Jeffrey was scheduled to appear in court on Sunday at the George Leighton Criminal Courthouse, 2650 S. California Ave.</p>

entries.title: 17-year-old boy charged following 19 burglaries on South, North sides
entries.summary: <p>A 17-year-old boy was arrested Saturday in connection with 19 burglaries spanning neighborhoods on the South and North sides, Chicago police said. </p><p>The boy was charged with 17 felony counts of burglary, one felony count of attempted burglary and one misdemeanor count of criminal damage to property, according to police. </p><p>Police say the boy is one of the people involved in the string of burglaries, which occurred in Lincoln Park, Ukrainian Village, Lake View, Roseland, Auburn Gresham, Beverly, Washington Heights, New City and Englewood. Twelve of the burglaries occurred on Oct. 15. The rest happened Oct. 16, Sept. 30 and May 7, police said. </p>

entries.title: Bears' next opponent: Saints stop 2-point conversion in OT to beat Browns 23-22
entries.summary: <p>NEW ORLEANS — Tyler Shough floated a 15-yard timing pass to Juwan Johnson toward the right corner of the end zone for a touchdown and the desperate New Orleans Saints stopped a do-or-die, 2-point conversion to outlast the Cleveland Browns 23-22 in overtime on Sunday.</p><p>After the Saints (3-5) scored on the first possession of overtime, Cleveland answered when Harold Fannin Jr. turned a short catch from Browns backup Shedeur Sanders into a tackle-breaking, 39-yard touchdown with a minute left in overtime.</p><p>The Browns (5-4) elected to try a 2-point conversion for the win, but Sanders was forced to roll right under pressure from Carl Granderson and threw incomplete along the sideline, giving the Saints their first win at home this season.</p><p>The thrilling finish followed a largely ugly first 54 minutes during which neither team scored a touchdown.</p><p>The Saints led 9-6 after Charlie Smyth — who made three of four field goal attempts after being elevated from the practice squad this week — split the uprights from 48 yards. But on Cleveland's next offensive play, Sanders spotted KC Concepcion Jr. running past cornerback Martin Emmerson Jr. down the right side and hit him for a 64-yard, go-ahead score with 5:33 left.</p><p>The Saints took a late 16-13 lead on newly reacquired running back Audric Estime's 2-yard touchdown with 58 seconds left in the fourth quarter, capping a 55-yard drive that began with 1:48 left.</p><p>But Sanders, with the help of a 30-yard completion to Jerry Jeudy, was able to move the Browns to the Saints 33 and set up Andre Szmyt's tying 51-yard field goal that sent the game to overtime.</p><p>Shough finished 21 of 35 for 265 yards and one TD. Chris Olave highlighted a seven-catch, 98-yard performance with a 33-yard reception to the 10-yard line to set up the late TD by Estime, who finished with 72 yards on 15 carries just five days after being claimed off of waivers.</p><p>Sanders was 19 of 31 for 297 yards and two TDs in his first start this season in place of Deshaun Watson, who sat out after spending part of the past week in the NFL's concussion protocol.</p><p>Denzel Boston caught six passes for 98 yards and Concepcion had four catches for 85 yards for Cleveland, which has lost its last two and three of four.</p><p>Poor red-zone execution by both teams left the game tied at 3 after the first half.</p><p>With two turnovers just minutes apart in the second quarter, the Saints went from being in position to take the lead to needing a big defensive stop to avoid falling behind.</p><p>New Orleans had just reached the Cleveland 11 on rookie Barion Brown's 52-yard catch when fellow rookie and first-round draft choice Jordyn Tyson followed two plays later with his first career reception inside the 5. But Tyson, making his NFL debut after missing the first seven games with a hamstring injury, fumbled at the 2 as he tried to dive for more yardage.</p><p>New Orleans' defense forced a quick punt, but Brown, after dancing away from pursuers during his return, fumbled when Adin Huntington caught him from behind near the Saints 20.</p><p>Donovan McMillon recovered for Cleveland, setting the Browns up to squander a scoring chance of their own when Quinshon Judkins was stopped on fourth-and-goal from the 1.</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Browns:</b> RG Austin Barber received treatment on the field for an apparent left leg injury. ... S Ronnie Hickman limped into the injury tent late in the fourth quarter.</p><p><b>Saints:</b> C Erik McCoy left with a biceps injury.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Browns:</b> Host the Houston Texans next Sunday.</p><p><b>Saints:</b> Host the Carolina Panthers next Sunday.<br></p>

entries.title: Blackhawks will make adjustments but no coaching changes after terrible start
entries.summary: <p>It turns out <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> coach Jeff Blashill was correct in his belief Saturday that he need not worry about his job security.</p><p>The Hawks are not going to make any coaching or staffing changes at this time, a source told the Sun-Times on Sunday, despite falling dramatically short of expectations so far this season.</p><p>However, members of the coaching staff, hockey operations department and team management held a series of meetings Sunday to determine what adjustments could be made, per the source.</p><p>General manager Kyle Davidson is scheduled to hold a news conference Wednesday to discuss the team's atrocious 4-13-1 start and his plans moving forward. The Hawks' next game is Thursday against the Sabres.</p><p>In the meantime, the team is scheduled to practice Monday, which could reveal some of the aforementioned adjustments to their systems or lineup. That practice will be followed by the annual season-ticket member party, which comes at an extremely awkward time Monday night.</p><p>"[These are] four days to regroup and just try to start a new season, almost," captain Connor Bedard said Saturday. "It’s almost 20 games in, and the season’s young. We’re not throwing the towel in or anything. We believe in ourselves."</p><p>Davidson has been reportedly active in trade negotiations, and news on that front could happen at any time. He might have an opportunity to do some negotiating in-person at a league-wide GM meeting Tuesday in Toronto.</p><p>The Hawks did indicate one upcoming change Sunday by placing beleaguered backup goalie Arvid Soderblom <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/08/blackhawks-backup-goalie-change-arvid-soderblom-waivers" >on waivers</a>, likely ending his run of more than three seasons in that role.</p>

entries.title: Lions grind past Dolphins for 19-9 victory
entries.summary: <p>MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. — The Detroit Lions have repeated a mantra all week in the aftermath of a scary neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell.</p><p>Play like No. 46.</p><p>They did that against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. Jahmyr Gibbs had a rushing touchdown, Jared Goff threw for 170 yards and the Lions beat the Dolphins 19-9 for their fourth straight victory.</p><p>"The whole week was prepare and play like Jack. Kind of felt like we owed it to him. It's all we can do," Detroit coach Dan Campbell said, adding later: "This was hard because you want to talk about it and acknowledge it. You don't want to brush it under the rug. That's not fair. The guy means too much to us. We bonded together and ultimately we found a way to win the game. It was emotional."</p><p>Jake Bates made four field goals on a day that was a bit underwhelming for Goff and the Lions' top-ranked offense, which entered averaging 29 points and 395.4 yards per game but finished with 271 yards.</p><p>Goff completed 17 of 25 passes while being sacked three times as Miami's defense pressured him throughout. Goff was intercepted by rookie cornerback Chris Johnson on a tipped pass in the first quarter — just the second pick he has thrown this season.</p><p>Gibbs averaged just 3.7 yards per carry, finishing with 74 yards on 20 attempts and an 8-yard rushing score that put the Lions ahead 16-6 entering the fourth. All-Pro Amon-Ra St. Brown had 86 yards receiving for the Lions, who are trying to keep pace in a tough NFC North.</p><p>Lions players arrived at Hard Rock Stadium wearing No. 46 jerseys to honor Jack Campbell, who was placed on injured reserve this week after he was hospitalized with the neck injury suffered during last Sunday's win over Minnesota.</p><p>Campbell's jersey was hanging in his locker at the stadium before the game, and some fans raised signs that read "Campbell Strong."</p><p>"That's a tough line you stand on — this balance beam of football and life and what really matters," edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson said. "For us to come out today and get the win with all that in our head and think about him while we're doing it, it's really important."</p><p>The Lions never trailed but could not pull away from the rebuilding Dolphins, who had been in four consecutive one-score games entering Sunday.</p><p>Bates made kicks of 28, 33, 40 and 43 yards. His 43-yarder gave Detroit a 10-point lead with 4:28 remaining.</p><p>The Lions led 9-6 with four minutes left in the third when Goff connected with Jameson Williams for a 31-yard pickup — Detroit's longest play of the game — that set up Gibbs' touchdown run on fourth down, his 11th scrimmage TD this season.</p><p>Then the Dolphins took a page out Dan Campbell's book of aggressive play-calling, executing a fake punt that gave Miami the ball at Detroit's 18, setting up a 34-yard field goal by Zane Gonzalez.</p><p>Malik Willis completed 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards and an interception while facing constant pressure from Detroit's front. Willis didn't use his legs as much as he has in previous games. He has a nagging groin injury and said after the game it "was a little tight."</p><p>The Dolphins went 0 for 3 in the red zone and failed to top 100 yards rushing for the second straight game. And despite staying within striking distance, the Dolphins had far too many self-inflicted wounds — including 11 penalties, a missed field goal and a kickoff that fell short of the landing zone.</p><p>"We can't keep saying the same things like, 'Oh, we've got to get better,'" Willis said. "We've got to continue to fight to actually do it and make sure that shows up on game day."</p><h3>Milestone for Dan Campbell</h3><p>Campbell picked up his 54th regular-season win as Detroit's coach, moving into second place alone in franchise history midway through his sixth season. Wayne Fontes is the Lions' winningest coach with 66 victories from 1988-96.</p><h3>Both teams run successful fake punts</h3><h3></h3><p>Dolphins punter Bradley Pinion connected with Kaytron Allen for a 46-yard completion on Miami's fourth-quarter fake punt.</p><p>"I'll take that. It was a good job by them," Dan Campbell said. "That certainly wasn't on our guys. That was on me."</p><p>In the second quarter, Jack Fox lined up to punt before tossing an 11-yard pass to Tay Martin, which gave Detroit the ball at the 41.</p><p>The Dolphins' defense held, though, sacking Goff on third down to force a real punt.</p><p>"Why did we give up the fake punt? We've got to go look back and make sure we're not giving anything away," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said. "They clearly saw something on tape that they took advantage of, just like we saw something on tape and we took advantage of it."</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Dolphins:</b> TE Will Kacmarek (quad) was injured on a low hit in the third quarter. He remained down for a couple of minutes before walking to the sideline unassisted.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Lions:</b> Travel to Germany, where they will face New England in Munich next Sunday.</p><p><b>Dolphins:</b> At Indianapolis next Sunday.<br></p>
